You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The unemployment rate of 8.2% with a falling trend, a fed funds rate of 0.13%, and a 10-year yield of 1.96% all point to early-to-mid 2012. The 10-year had dropped to about 1.96% by late May 2012 (it was roughly 1.6% by then), so I checked the month more carefully.

- The 10-year yield was about 2.2% in March 2012, and about 1.8% in April.
- Unemployment was 8.2% in March and April 2012, and 8.1% in May.
- The VIX was 16.3, and equities fell 0.3% over the month. The S&P was down about 0.75% in April 2012 and down about 6% in May, so April fits better than May.
- The 20y+ Treasury return of +3.1% over 1m suggests yields fell sharply. A 10-year yield of 1.96% fits the end of April 2012, when it was about 1.95%.
- Payroll growth averaged 211k over three months (Jan–Mar 2012 was roughly 275k, 220k, 143k). A 3-month change of +47 would fit the data as of April 2012.
- Headline CPI of 2.65% fits March 2012 (2.7%), which was published in April, and core CPI of 2.25% also fits.
- Developed ex-US equity was down 12.6% over 12 months, which fits the euro crisis period.
- The dollar was up 14% over 12 months, which fits the 2011–12 period.

This leads to April 2012.
